first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly, top to bottom on the iPad. The opening is calm and grown-up. I liked being told where the information comes from rather than being handed a list of five things. The headline asking what I 'did not know' felt a little like a magazine teaser, but the page itself is not like that.

journey.quote: This guide follows the order of a real celebration and traces each meaning to UNESCO, museum dress collections and named reference works. Where a story is only "often told", we say so.
journey.reaction: Good. I would rather be told honestly what is lore and what is fact. That makes me trust the rest.

journey.quote: there is no single correct version, only the version your families recognise.
journey.reaction: A relief, frankly. I was worried about getting something wrong in front of the other family. This tells me to ask them, which is exactly what I would do.

journey.quote: Palestinian weddings do not happen in a single day. Ceremonies often run over several days, sometimes a week
journey.reaction: Several days, possibly a week. As the person paying half, my first thought is how many evenings, venues and caterers that means. The page explains the customs well but never helps me think about what several events cost or how they are organised.

journey.quote: If you are marrying in Australia, the religious contract and the Australian legal marriage are separate steps, so plan both.
journey.reaction: Useful and practical. That is the kind of thing I would want flagged, and I will mention it to my husband.

journey.quote: On the main garment, the loose-fitting dress called a thob, the chest, sleeves and cuffs are embroidered, with vertical panels running down from the waist, worked in silk thread on wool, linen or cotton.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but this section goes on. Five or six paragraphs of museum detail. I read it, but on the iPad it started to feel like a textbook. I only need to know the dress may take months to make, and that comes later.

journey.section: Bringing these customs to your destination wedding
journey.quote: As at 1 November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians not to travel to Palestine
journey.reaction: Thank you. This is the first thing I would have worried about, and it is dealt with plainly, with a date and the government source. That is responsible.

journey.section: Bringing these customs to your destination wedding
journey.quote: Dabke is danced in a line, with jumping and stamping, so you need length and a firm surface rather than a small square in front of the band.
journey.reaction: The checklist is the best part for me. Real, practical questions to put to a venue. But nothing in it is about the older guests. If this runs several nights, my mother needs seating, a quiet room and a way to the terrace without stairs.

journey.section: Bringing these customs to your destination wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the venue's sound limits, floor size and finishing time in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'In writing' is the phrase I was looking for. That tells me someone is accountable. I would like the same promise about deposits and contracts, though, and it is not there.

journey.section: Bringing these customs to your destination wedding
journey.quote: Others travel further: the United Arab Emirates, for example, is at "Exercise a high degree of caution" on Smartraveller
journey.reaction: If the couple did go overseas, this is where I want to know about insurance, transfers and who I ring when something goes wrong. The page stops at the travel advice level.

journey.quote: When you are ready to plan, a Wedded Advisor will listen to how your families celebrate and build the days around it.
journey.reaction: Warm, and I like that it is a person. But I do not know if 'speak with' means a phone call or a form, and I would want a phone call before anything is booked.

unanswered_questions: Is a Wedded Advisor a named person I can ring, and is the first conversation a phone call?
Who holds the deposits for a multi-event wedding, and are they protected?
Are contracts and quotes in Australian dollars and in English, even for an overseas venue?
How do you look after elderly guests across several late nights: seating, accessibility, transfers, a quiet room?
Who is responsible on the night if a supplier lets us down, and who do I call?
If several evenings are needed (henna night, sahra, wedding), do you coordinate all of them or only the main day?
Is travel insurance something you advise on for guests if the couple marry overseas?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Palestinian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly clickbait in tone. Minor, the page underneath is sensible.

turn_offs_found.quote: UNESCO describes a practice that began in rural areas and is now common across Palestine and among the diaspora. Women's village clothing usually comprised a long dress, trousers, jacket, headdress and veil, each embroidered with birds, trees and flowers.
turn_offs_found.why: The tatreez section is a run of dense paragraphs. Readable, but long for a screen. Not a deal breaker.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like help shaping these evenings into one plan, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
turn_offs_found.why: This is the only mention of help, and it says nothing about contracts, deposits or who is responsible. That is one of my turn-offs, though only partly, because the 'in writing' line just before it helps.

would_share_with: My husband, with a note about the separate religious and legal steps and the several-night schedule
The groom's mother, to check which customs their family keeps

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to plan, a Wedded Advisor will listen to how your families celebrate and build the days around it.
cta_reaction.why: It is my daughter's decision to enquire, not mine. I would click to see whether it leads to a phone number and a named person. If it is just a form with no word on deposits or who is accountable, I would leave it to her.

top_3_changes: Add one or two lines on older guests across several nights (seating, step-free access, a quiet room, transfers) to the venue checklist.
Extend the 'in writing' line to say who is accountable and how deposits and contracts are handled (AUD, English), without needing prices.
Make the Advisor CTA say plainly that it starts with a conversation with a named person, ideally by phone, and trim the tatreez section by a paragraph or two.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom)
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Absence of prices and deferred business details not treated as must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional (assumed, not CRM-calibrated). Weight Margaret's elderly-guest and deposit concerns accordingly.
Does the Wedded Advisor CTA lead to a phone call option or only a form? A funding parent wants a phone call first.

assumptions: Margaret is reading because her daughter is marrying into, or is part of, a Palestinian-heritage family; the page does not need to address which.
Per orchestrator, business details (fees, deposits policy specifics) are deferred and no prices is the standard, so these are logged as unanswered, not must-fix.
